exercise.name: High Knees
library_steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Run on the spot, driving each knee up to hip height.
Pump your arms and land softly on the balls of your feet.
exercise.one_line_summary: Running on the spot, trunk tall. Picture 1: left knee driven up to about hip height (hip ~80 deg, knee ~90 deg) while standing on the ball of the right foot, right arm forward and left arm back; picture 2: the mirror.

setup.target: Feet hip-width; stay in one spot.
setup.why: Library step; S2 cue to stay in place.

setup.target: Upright, core braced, no slouch or lean back.

movement.tolerance: 70-95 (S2: hip height is as high as needed)

movement.start: knee ~25 deg, on the ball of the foot (heel up ~25 deg)

movement.measure: elev / plane / elbow (opposite arm to the lifted knee goes forward)

movement.start: +0.03 m (up on the ball of the foot)

muscles.emg: Quadriceps active around foot strike and support in jogging, running and sprinting (S1 Fig. 3)
muscles.role: Library primary is 'cardio' (no muscle). For the picture the front thigh is lit: rectus femoris helps lift the knee and the quads absorb each landing. Library lists quads as secondary.

muscles.emg: Gastrocnemius active late swing through support at all speeds (S1 Fig. 3)
muscles.role: Land and push off on the ball of the foot; library secondary.

muscles.emg: Fine-wire iliacus active from just after toe-off through forward swing, longer at higher speed (S1)
muscles.role: Main knee-drive muscle; lies deep in the pelvis, so not lit.

muscles.emg: Late swing and early support activity (S1)
muscles.role: Hold the pelvis on the stance leg.

muscles.emg: Consistent only in sprinting, around toe-off and early swing (S1)

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to get the knee higher
mistakes.why_it_matters: S2: stay upright, no slouching or leaning back.
Library: land softly on the balls of the feet.

sources.citation: Moran GT, Mann RA, Dougherty SE, Moran SA. Biomechanics of running: electromyographic analysis of the hip during jogging, running and sprinting. ISBS Conference Proceedings Archive, pp. 439-446.
sources.what_it_gave: 15 trained sprinters: swing-phase hip flexion ~40 deg jogging, 60 running, 80 sprinting; iliacus (fine wire) active after toe-off through forward swing; quadriceps, gastrocnemius, gluteal timing.

sources.citation: The Prehab Guys. Exercise library: High Knees - In Place.
sources.what_it_gave: Knee as high as tolerated, hip level is enough; upright trunk, core on, no slouch or lean back; push off the opposite toes; stay in one spot.

clip_check.check: Stance foot: ball on the floor, heel up
Arm opposite the lifted knee is the forward arm
Quads are the strongest red in both pictures
